items.title: Supreme Court refuses to halt forensic audit of Fortis transactions in Daiichi-Singh brothers dispute

However, a Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana clarified that the High Court's observations against Fortis were only tentative and prima facie and would not bind the forensic auditor. The forensic audit will have to be conducted independently without being influenced by those observations. “It goes without saying that the forensic audit shall be conducted independently without being influenced by those observations made by the High Court, ” the Court added. The proceedings arose out of Daiichi Sankyo's efforts to enforce a 2016 arbitral award against the Singh brothers and other judgment debtors. The dispute subsequently expanded to examine what happened to the Singh brothers' substantial shareholding in Fortis while proceedings were pending before courts. According to the submissions before the Supreme Court, the Singh brothers earlier controlled around 70 percent of Fortis. Their shareholding subsequently fell sharply
